Build the Bowditch midpoint-operation disk G(m,n): the first/last row cyclic vertices bound it, intermediate triangles follow consecutive midpoint rows, and a final fan caps the last small polygon. Assign each triangle its spherical comparison metric when inequalities are strict. The map from the disk graph to X is distance-nonincreasing, because each face perimeter<2l permits local comparison. At each interior row vertex v, its images are the midpoint of adjacent prior-row v1,v2; hence ρ(v1,v2)≥d(gv1,gv2)=ρ(v1,v)+ρ(v,v2), and triangle inequality forces equality and cone angle≥2pi. Last-row boundary angles are≥pi, first-row angles<pi. Finite cellulation induction excludes simple closed local geodesics: a curve outside the first-row vertices would have to remain inside a comparison triangle in an open hemisphere. The compact local CAT(1) short-circle criterion then makes this disk pi-CAT(1). Prove Bowditch3.3.10 quantitatively: for loop length2r<2pi split at arclength r with endpoints y,z and chord midpoint a. For any point x write b=d(x,y),d=d(x,z),c=d(y,z); b+d≤r and c≥|b−d|. Spherical midpoint comparison gives cos d(a,x)≥(cos b+cos d)/(2cos(c/2))≥cos(r/2), so radius≤R=r/2=pi/2−η with η=(pi−r)/2. At a radius-maximizing boundary vertex x and equal outgoing segments of length μ=min{r/(2n),η}, two endpoint distances to a are≤D=d(a,x)≤R. Glue the spherical comparison triangles on opposite sides of ax; their perimeters are≤2R+μ<pi because μ≤η. The spherical cosine law makes each direction angle at x strictly below pi/2, so the intrinsic quadrilateral distance d_Q(y,z)<2μ by an explicit local corner shortcut near x. On the compact parameter family satisfying these inequalities and μ>0, this strict defect has a positive continuous minorant δ(η,μ); prove continuity by the two finite spherical triangles and their chord-or-via-apex shortest-path cases, including collapsed triangles, with μ<2η excluding the equality corner. This is the source quadrilateral constant. Ambient sphere chord distance is not substituted for d_Q unless the chord lies in Q. Obtain the estimate for longer unequal midpoint segments by selecting the initial equal μ pieces and adding the remaining lengths. Treat D=0 as an impossible nonconstant configuration. The source compact-family constant and the explicit radiusη feed the exact energy inequality. items.contract: Prove local CAT(1) of the l2 product without importing smooth-manifold comparison. Project a sufficiently small product triangle to its factor triangles and pair their S² comparison triangles at proportional side parameters; their boundary maps bound original product distances. It suffices to prove model S²×S² vertex-side comparison (a Euclidean factor has the stronger zero-curvature formula). Along a constant-speed model product geodesic use factor speeds v_i, radial distances r_i from a fixed product vertex, R²=Σr_i²,V²=Σv_i² and f(u)=u cot u, f(0)=1. On 0<r_i<pi derive r_i″=cot(r_i)(v_i²−(r_i′)²) by twice differentiating the spherical cosine formula. Because f decreases and |r_i′|≤v_i, sum to obtain RR″−f(R)(V²−(R′)²)≥(1−f(R))(Σ(r_i′)²−(R′)²)≥0 by Cauchy. Thus F=cos R satisfies F″+V²F≤0. Triangle perimeter<2pi bounds R(t) by min{a+tV,b+(1−t)V}<pi, excluding factor antipodes. Sine Green-kernel comparison on V<pi gives F(t)≥[sin((1−t)V)cos a+sin(tV)cos b]/sin V, the spherical vertex-side inequality. Prove the scalar comparison directly by the positive Dirichlet kernel or interior-minimum test and sine addition formulas. At r_i=0 use smooth squared spherical distance and continuity; cos sqrt(q) is smooth at q=0. Alexandrov subdivisions give all side-point comparisons, and paired factor-model boundary maps give the asserted product inequality on uniform local charts. No distributions, Riemannian curvature theorem or CAT(0) squared-distance surrogate is required.

Set η=η(π−r) from the comparison disk radius lemma and μ=min{r/(2n),η}, meeting μ<2η. The radius-maximizing boundary point lies on the first row (last-row angles≥pi), so the quadrilateral estimate gives one ζ_k≤(ξ_k+ξ_(k+1))/2−δ(η,μ). Choose δ no larger than this average. Its square deficit is≥δ(ξ_k+ξ_(k+1))/2≥δ r/n. Thus Δ≥λ_n(L), where a safe continuous positive choice is half min{r²/n⁴,δ(η(π−r),min(r/(2n),η(π−r))) r/n}. On a compact length band [a,b]⊂(0,2pi), λ has a positive minimum and E≤b², so after at most ceil(b²/minλ)+1 iterates every basin tuple has length<a. Hence the zero-limit basin is closed as well as open in the fixed-n short-polygon space. It cannot contain an equally spaced local-geodesic tuple. Its regular point has trivial W stabilizer, so the color-dihedral action on the plane is faithful. If h=ord(c), θ=kπ/h; its 2h chamber sectors have disjoint interiors, giving θ≤π/h and k=1. Every root wall meets this plane in a boundary line. At a fundamental boundary ray the zero set is exactly J or K; W_J or W_K is an independent commuting-reflection group, whose only rank-one reflections are its simple generators. Transport to every ray: no extra root walls occur. A half-turn crosses every positive wall once; expanding alternating color blocks yields a reduced word by the root-sign length criterion and precisely the prefix roots ρ_i without repeats. If h even, there are h/2 blocks of each color. If h odd, a,b are dihedrally conjugate, so their (-1)-eigenspace dimensions |J|,|K| agree; the total letter count is again nh/2. Hence Φ_+=(ρ_1,...,ρ_(nh/2)); the word is w0, equal to c^(h/2) for even h and c^((h-1)/2)a for odd h. Prove c-1 invertible separately from (c-1)β_i=-2ρ_i and triangular independence for 1≤i≤n.
